## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Firecrawl
Authenticated search combines web results, semantic tool summaries and domain matches. Use sources: ["alexandria"] for semantic tools only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. Tool matches describe available structured-data capabilities, not executed data. toolDetail: "compact" (default) returns only provider, capability and description; "summary" adds metadata; "full" includes their input and output contracts. firecrawl_scrape with an alexandria body executes a selected capability; firecrawl_find_tools provides catalogue browsing and full contracts. Firecrawl provides web, developer, government, and research search, and executes catalogued Alexandria data providers. Use firecrawl_search to find relevant results across the web and specialized indexes; authenticated searches also return matching Alexandria providers in data.tools. firecrawl_find_tools provides catalogue browsing and provider contracts; firecrawl_scrape with an alexandria body executes a selected capability; firecrawl_scrape with a url retrieves one supplied page. For a programming question, firecrawl_developer_search searches indexed public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, READMEs, and code documentation and returns the matched passages, and skills: "only" narrows it to agent-skill files; firecrawl_search with categories: ["developer"] reaches the same index beside ordinary web results, returning the hits in the web group rather than as passages and offering no skills filter. For a legal or regulatory question, firecrawl_gov_search searches primary law and regulatory material from US federal, state, and local government sources: statutes, regulations, codes, court opinions, and other government publications; firecrawl_search with categories: ["gov"] reaches the same sources in the web group and cannot be combined with other categories. For a biomedical, life-science, clinical, or arXiv literature question, the firecrawl_research_* tools search the paper index, while categories: ["research"] on firecrawl_search filters ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites. Use the firecrawl_research_* tools to search academic and research literature, expand from anchor papers via the citation graph, and read full-text passages from a specific paper. Search and discovery tools are read-only and return ranked results. firecrawl_search_feedback records a quality rating for a prior firecrawl_search by its id. Billing: web, developer, and research search are billed per request; government search is free; Alexandria discovery (firecrawl_search with sources ["alexandria"] alone, and firecrawl_find_tools) is free; firecrawl_scrape is billed, as a page retrieval in url mode or at each executed capability's listed price in alexandria mode.

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. # Tool paths (macOS)

The lookup table. Read this when you need a path; the **traps** that must be known
without looking stay in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `~/.claude/AGENTS.md`.

**Verified 2026-09-05** with `which -a python3 uv go node npm claude codex pwsh`.

| Tool | Path | Note |
|---|---|---|
| python3 | `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3` | 3.14, PEP 668-managed. `/usr/bin/python3` is the system copy — Homebrew's wins on PATH. |
| uv / uvx | `/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/uv` | Standalone install, `uv self update`. **Not** Homebrew. |
| go | `/opt/homebrew/bin/go` | |
| node | `/opt/homebrew/bin/node` | |
| npm / npx | `/opt/homebrew/bin/` | |
| claude | `/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/claude` | |
| codex | `/opt/homebrew/bin/codex` | |
| pwsh | `/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh` | PowerShell 7. Present only to run the KeystoneOS `.ps1` jobs natively. |
| Go-installed CLIs | `/Users/kristinarash/go/bin/` | `fireflies-pp-cli`, `espn-pp-cli`, and the other `*-pp-cli` tools. |

`uv` and `claude` each resolve twice under `which -a` — they sit in PATH twice, not in
two locations. Same binary, so it is harmless; do not "fix" it by deleting one.

## Secrets

Secrets live in the macOS Keychain, never in `~/.zshrc`. Read one with:

```bash
security find-generic-password -s FIREFLIES_API_KEY -a "$USER" -w
```

## History that explains the layout

- `/usr/local/bin` is **empty and stays that way.** Homebrew owns `/opt/homebrew/bin`.
- Docker Desktop, and the `kubectl` it shipped, was removed 2026-09-03. Nothing here used it.

## Why this file exists

This table used to sit in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, which loads into every session in every
project — paying for the whole list on every turn to answer a question asked on a few of
them. `AGENTS.md` had already refused to carry a second copy for the same reason. Now both
files carry the traps and point here for the lookup.

**Re-verify before trusting a row.** Tools have existed in two places before, with the older
one winning. `which -a <tool>` is authoritative, and this file is a snapshot with a date on it.

description: "PATH shadowing repair 2026-08-13 — measure PATH with env -i, grep hardcoded paths before deleting a binary, broken symlinks evade find -type f"
metadata:

Repairs made 2026-08-13 on this Mac, and the four traps hit doing it. All four generalise.

**What was wrong and is now fixed:**
- `uv` existed twice — `~/.local/bin/uv` 0.11.6 (Apr) shadowed Homebrew's 0.12.1 (Jul), so a
  three-month-old build was winning. Fixed with `uv self update` → 0.12.3, then `brew uninstall uv`.
- PATH had duplicate `~/go/bin` and `~/.local/bin` entries (17 entries → 15). Sources: a redundant
  export in `.zshrc`, a duplicated `go/bin` line, and two unguarded `brew shellenv` calls in `.zprofile`.
- An entire pre-migration Node install at `/usr/local` (~690 MB: node, npm, npx, corepack, stale
  codex/gemini/gws) removed. `/usr/local/bin` now holds only Docker Desktop + kubectl.
- `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` moved from plaintext in `.zshrc` into the login Keychain.

**The four traps — these are the reusable part:**

1. **A PATH read from inside a tool shell is a lie.** Any earlier `export PATH=…` in the session
   pollutes it. This produced a wrong claim (`~/.bun/bin` reported as duplicated when it was not).
   Honest measurement:
   `env -i HOME="$HOME" USER="$USER" TERM=xterm SHELL=/bin/zsh /bin/zsh -lic 'echo $PATH'`
2. **PATH order only governs lookups by name.** Deleting `~/.local/bin/uv` would have silently
   killed three hooks in `~/.claude/settings.json` (SessionStart/PreCompact/SessionEnd) that call
   the memory-compiler by *absolute path*. Always `grep -rl '/full/path' ~/.claude ~/DEV` first.
3. **Scheduled jobs are the blind spot.** Eight KeystoneOS launchd agents referenced `/usr/local`
   — harmlessly, as PATH entries — but nothing in shell config would have shown them. Check
   `~/Library/LaunchAgents` before touching a shared prefix.
4. **`[ -e ]` and `find -type f` both skip broken symlinks.** 92 npm man pages were symlinks into
   a just-deleted tree; the first cleanup pass removed 1 of 92 and reported success. Use
   `find … \( -type l -o -type f \) -delete`.

**Still open (his action):** rotate the Fireflies key — the old value persists in two `.zshrc`
backups, session transcripts, and `~/.claude/file-history/`; the Keychain does not retract those.
Also `sudo rm -rf /usr/local/include/node` (62 MB) and `sudo rmdir /usr/local/lib/node_modules`.

**Why:** each of these cost real debugging time, and three of them fail *silently* — the wrong
version runs, the hook stops, the file never gets deleted, with no error.
**How to apply:** before asserting where a tool lives or deleting any binary on this machine, run
the `env -i` measurement and the hardcoded-path grep. See also [[zsh-shell-traps]] and
[[terminal-fluency-workspace]].

input.summary: The toolchain itself is in good shape. uv is a single copy at ~/.local/bin/uv, Homebrew Python is clean, every launchd interpreter and venv exists, gh auth is valid, FileVault and SIP are on, and macOS is current. The real problem is the machine. It has 8 GB of RAM, 94% of swap is used, load is 6 to 9.5, and four Claude sessions each run their own copy of the MCP servers. Smaller exposures: the firewall is off, there is no Time Machine, a plaintext MODEL_ROUTER_KEY sits in ~/.zshrc for a dead router, the Fireflies key still has not been rotated, PowerShell comes from a deprecated tap, and a false dcg "Hook missing" warning prints in every shell.

findings.title: 8 GB Mac is swapping hard: 94% of swap used, 58M swap-ins in under 3 days, load average 6-9.5
findings.evidence: sysctl vm.swapusage -> 'total = 9216.00M used = 8659.81M free = 556.19M'; memory_pressure -> 'Swapins: 57876418 / Swapouts: 61578748'; sysctl hw.memsize = 8589934592; uptime -> 'up 2 days, 20:16, 3 users, load averages: 5.96 9.55 9.37'. ps shows 4 root claude processes (pids 35034, 75119, 4638, plus ClaudeCode.app children). Two sessions are 14h old (75119, 79892/80001 bg-spare 166 MB RSS). There are 39 node processes, including three full duplicate MCP sets (context-mode start.mjs x3, playwright-mcp x3, desktop-commander x3, mcp-pdf-server x2, codex app-server). Google Drive.app used 148:13 CPU-min over 3:57:47 elapsed (about 62% of a core sustained). trustd used 49:22 CPU-min over 9:20 elapsed. everythingd was at 48.8% when sampled.
findings.impact: Under this much memory pressure every hook, launchd job and agent session runs slower. That plausibly feeds the known memsearch hook timeouts (memory project_memsearch-hook-timeout-cap.md), but this audit did not verify the link. Long-idle sessions and their duplicated MCP servers hold memory that is never given back.
findings.fix: Close idle Claude Code sessions (two are 14h old) and keep about 2 running at once on this 8 GB machine. Check whether all of context-mode, playwright, desktop-commander and pdf-viewer need to load in every session, and disable the plugins not used daily. Find out why Google Drive.app is averaging about 62% CPU; it may be catching up after the trash wave. Long term, the memory ceiling is the bottleneck for running agents in parallel on this machine.

findings.title: macOS application firewall is disabled; Apple services listen on all interfaces
findings.evidence: /usr/libexec/ApplicationFirewall/socketfilterfw --getglobalstate -> 'Firewall is disabled. (State = 0)'; stealth mode off. lsof -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN shows ControlCenter on *:5000 and *:7000 (AirPlay Receiver) and rapportd on *:60109. Eric's own services are correctly bound to loopback: board.py on 127.0.0.1:7474, Logi on 127.0.0.1.
findings.impact: The laptop joins campus and public networks with no inbound filtering. Right now that exposes only Apple services, but any future dev server bound to 0.0.0.0 would be reachable from the network at once.
findings.fix: Turn on the firewall in System Settings > Network > Firewall (or sudo socketfilterfw --setglobalstate on). Optionally enable stealth mode and switch off AirPlay Receiver if it is not used.

findings.title: No Time Machine destination; nothing can restore the whole machine
findings.evidence: tmutil destinationinfo -> 'tmutil: No destinations configured.'; tmutil latestbackup -> 'Failed to mount backup destination ... Code=17'. ~/.claude/scripts/logs/daily-backup.out 2026-10-22 05:48:13: 'TARGET SSD /Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup NOT MOUNTED ... SKIPPED this run'; 06:05:12 'daily-backup end: ERROR (5 errors)'. launchctl list shows com.keystone.dailybackup last exit 1.
findings.impact: Recovery depends on the custom Drive and CRASHBOX design. That design covers chosen paths, not the system, apps, Keychain or app settings, and its SSD leg is usually skipped. A disk failure would mean a manual rebuild of the toolchain.
findings.fix: Decide on purpose whether to add Time Machine (for example a partition on CRASHBOX or another disk) as the whole-machine layer, or record in STORAGE.md Known gaps that whole-machine restore is out of scope. The daily-backup 5 errors belong to the backup domain audit.
findings.known_where: The CRASHBOX-unmounted gap is known (STATUS.md:201, memory project_backup-sync-system.md). The missing Time Machine is not recorded.

findings.title: Plaintext MODEL_ROUTER_KEY in ~/.zshrc for a model-router that nothing uses and that is not running
findings.evidence: ~/.zshrc:38 'export MODEL_ROUTER_KEY="<literal, ~45 chars>"' (value not printed), with MODEL_ROUTER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8317 (lines 36-40, 'added 2026-08-15'). lsof shows nothing listening on 8317 and no router process is running. rg for 'MODEL_ROUTER_' over ~/.claude, ~/DEV and ~/go/src found no references. ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and machine.md say 'Secrets live in the macOS Keychain, not in ~/.zshrc.'
findings.impact: Breaks the house secrets rule. The key is exported to every child process, including every agent session and its tools, and it is captured in any dotfile backup or shell snapshot. The config is otherwise dead.
findings.fix: Remove the four MODEL_ROUTER_* exports from ~/.zshrc. If the router comes back, store the key with security add-generic-password -s MODEL_ROUTER_KEY and read it in the launching script, as .zshenv does for TYPESAFE_API_KEY. Rotate the key at the proxy if it was ever used against a real upstream.

findings.title: Old Fireflies API key literal still in a .zshrc backup; rotation still open since 2026-08-13
findings.evidence: ~/.zshrc.bak-20260813-prekeychain:26 'export FIREFLIES_API_KEY="<literal>"' (mode -rw-------). ~/.zshrc.bak-20260813-preflight also has 1 FIREFLIES line. Keychain entry FIREFLIES_API_KEY exists.
findings.impact: The old key is still on disk, and the memory note says it is also in transcripts and file-history. It stays valid until it is rotated.
findings.fix: Rotate the key in the Fireflies dashboard, update it with security add-generic-password -U, then delete the two .zshrc.bak-20260813-* files.

findings.title: PowerShell is installed from the deprecated powershell/tap, which will be disabled 2027-06-18; 6 KeystoneOS launchd jobs depend on it
findings.evidence: brew doctor: 'Some installed formulae are deprecated or disabled ... powershell'. brew info powershell: 'powershell/tap/powershell 7.5.2 ... Deprecated because it is now maintained by Homebrew Core ... It will be disabled on 2027-06-18'; 'Warning: `powershell` shadows `homebrew/core/powershell`'. Launch agents adjudicate, agysync, morning, reconcile, rituals and stackdoctor run /opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh; dailybackup runs it through caffeinate.
findings.impact: This copy gets no more updates now, and after the disable date it can break on a brew upgrade. If it does, the KeystoneOS jobs stop.
findings.fix: Plan a swap to the core formula: brew uninstall powershell/tap/powershell && brew untap powershell/tap && brew install powershell. Then confirm /opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh still exists and kick one job by hand. Do this when Eric is at the machine.

findings.title: The dcg check in ~/.zshrc warns 'Hook missing' in every shell, but the hook is installed
findings.evidence: Clean login shell prints '[dcg] Hook missing from ~/.claude/settings.json — run: dcg install'. The check at ~/.zshrc:44-46 uses jq test("dcg\"?$"), but the installed PreToolUse hook command is 'if [ -x "$HOME/.local/bin/dcg" ]; then exec "$HOME/.local/bin/dcg"; else cat >/dev/null; fi', which ends in 'fi'. The strict jq check exits 4; a loose match for 'dcg' finds 1 hook.
findings.impact: A false alarm on every terminal trains Eric to ignore it, so a real removal would go unnoticed. Following its advice (dcg install) could rewrite the custom guarded hook in settings.json.
findings.fix: Change the regex in ~/.zshrc to test("\\.local/bin/dcg") (or simply test("dcg")). Do not run dcg install.

findings.title: GitHub MCP server loads with an unset GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN and fails every session, though settings disable it
findings.evidence: This session: 'plugin:github:github (400): Authorization header is badly formatted'. ~/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/github/c2bdb427efe8/.mcp.json sends 'Authorization: Bearer ${GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN}', and that variable is unset. ~/.claude/settings.json and ~/.claude/settings.local.json:23 both set github@claude-plugins-official=false. ~/.claude.json also lists github@synced and github@inline usage entries; this audit could not find which source enabled it.
findings.impact: A connection fails at every start (noise and startup time). Any skill expecting GitHub MCP tools silently falls back. The gh CLI still works.
findings.fix: Find which source enables github@synced or github@inline (claude.ai synced plugins or the workflow/inline plugin set) and disable it there. Alternatively, supply the token from Keychain through a wrapper.

data.summary: The toolchain itself is in good shape. uv is a single copy at ~/.local/bin/uv, Homebrew Python is clean, every launchd interpreter and venv exists, gh auth is valid, FileVault and SIP are on, and macOS is current. The real problem is the machine. It has 8 GB of RAM, 94% of swap is used, load is 6 to 9.5, and four Claude sessions each run their own copy of the MCP servers. Smaller exposures: the firewall is off, there is no Time Machine, a plaintext MODEL_ROUTER_KEY sits in ~/.zshrc for a dead router, the Fireflies key still has not been rotated, PowerShell comes from a deprecated tap, and a false dcg "Hook missing" warning prints in every shell.

findings.title: 8 GB Mac is swapping hard: 94% of swap used, 58M swap-ins in under 3 days, load average 6-9.5
findings.evidence: sysctl vm.swapusage -> 'total = 9216.00M used = 8659.81M free = 556.19M'; memory_pressure -> 'Swapins: 57876418 / Swapouts: 61578748'; sysctl hw.memsize = 8589934592; uptime -> 'up 2 days, 20:16, 3 users, load averages: 5.96 9.55 9.37'. ps shows 4 root claude processes (pids 35034, 75119, 4638, plus ClaudeCode.app children). Two sessions are 14h old (75119, 79892/80001 bg-spare 166 MB RSS). There are 39 node processes, including three full duplicate MCP sets (context-mode start.mjs x3, playwright-mcp x3, desktop-commander x3, mcp-pdf-server x2, codex app-server). Google Drive.app used 148:13 CPU-min over 3:57:47 elapsed (about 62% of a core sustained). trustd used 49:22 CPU-min over 9:20 elapsed. everythingd was at 48.8% when sampled.
findings.impact: Under this much memory pressure every hook, launchd job and agent session runs slower. That plausibly feeds the known memsearch hook timeouts (memory project_memsearch-hook-timeout-cap.md), but this audit did not verify the link. Long-idle sessions and their duplicated MCP servers hold memory that is never given back.
findings.fix: Close idle Claude Code sessions (two are 14h old) and keep about 2 running at once on this 8 GB machine. Check whether all of context-mode, playwright, desktop-commander and pdf-viewer need to load in every session, and disable the plugins not used daily. Find out why Google Drive.app is averaging about 62% CPU; it may be catching up after the trash wave. Long term, the memory ceiling is the bottleneck for running agents in parallel on this machine.

findings.title: macOS application firewall is disabled; Apple services listen on all interfaces

(State = 0)'; stealth mode off. lsof -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN shows ControlCenter on *:5000 and *:7000 (AirPlay Receiver) and rapportd on *:60109. findings.fix: Turn on the firewall in System Settings > Network > Firewall (or sudo socketfilterfw --setglobalstate on). Optionally enable stealth mode and switch off AirPlay Receiver if it is not used.
